chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Munzir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Three are there for whom a Prayer is not accepted: an absconder slave from his masters until he places his hand in their hands, and a woman who spent the night while her husband was angry with her, and a man who leads a group in prayer while they are displeased with him.

key_terms.عَبْدٌ آبِقٌ: An absconder slave who has run away from his master

ai.seo_question: What are the three conditions that invalidate a person's prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights three specific conditions that invalidate the acceptance of prayer (salat), emphasizing the interplay between ritual purity and social harmony in Shia jurisprudence. It specifically notes that a slave must be physically returned to his master, a wife must reconcile with her husband if he is displeased, and an imam must be acceptable to his congregation, reflecting the principle that spiritual validity is often contingent upon rectifying interpersonal rights (huquq al-nas).

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban Bin Usman, from Al Hassan Bin Munzir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There are three for whom a Prayer is not Accepted – and absconder from his master until (he returns and) places his hand in his hand, and a woman irrevocably divorced and her husband is angered upon her, and a man who leads a group of people (in Prayer) and they are disliking him’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from al-Hassan ibn al-Mundhir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Salat (prayer) of three kinds of people is not accepted. One is a runaway slave from his masters until he places his hand in their hands, a woman who passes the night when her husband is angry with her and a man who leads a people in Salat (prayer) and they dislike him.’”
